title.narrative: European Commission World Bank Partnership Programme Part III for Europe and Central Asia Programmatic Trust Fund

description.narrative:
"The objective of the Trust Fund is to support the Government of Kosovo to increase the efficiency of water utilization and boost agriculture productivity in the project area.
1.1 Introduction The EC and the WB share a common vision of building competitive andsustainable economies and in reducing poverty and social exclusion.These goals are outlined in the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework(MFF) (2014-2020) - ""The EU as a global player"" and in the proposed MFFfor 2021-2027 - ""Neighbourhood and the World"". The MFFs are designed toallow the Union to fulfil its responsibility both at global level andin its immediate Neighbourhoodcomma and to help safeguard global publicgoodscomma i.e.comma fighting poverty and promoting democracycomma peace commastabilitycomma and prosperity. The MFF 2014-2020 supports the EC's approach under the ""Agenda forChange""comma to focus EU aid in fewer sectors supportingcomma inter aliacomma goodgovernance and creating inclusive and sustainable growth. In thecontext of the establishment of the Part III - EEPP programcomma it isimportant to take into account the new MFF which has been presented bythe EC on May 2comma 2018. In factcomma the program will ideally coincide withthe timeframe of the current and next proposed MFF for 2021-2027. Thelatter will be guided by the EU's new consensus for developmentcomma which aims to fostersustainable development by focusing on cross-cutting elements ofdevelopment policy such as gender equalitycomma youthcomma investment andtradecomma sustainable energy and climate actioncomma good governance commademocracycomma rule of law and human rightscomma and migration and mobility. A continued constrained growth and a tight fiscal environment in theNeighbourhoodcomma Western Balkanscomma Turkeycomma and Central Asia make itimportant for the EC and the World Bank to coordinate policy advice commawhere appropriatecomma and to allocate their resources in the region in themost strategic and effective way possible. As a resultcomma the EC and theWorld Bank have begun since 2011 to interact more directly by means ofa programmatic TF to support the Europe 2020 Agendacomma which has allowed the World Bank to engage directly with individual European countries onprojects that are financed by the governments entirely or in part by EUExternal Action Instruments and other EU resourcescomma such as theStructural Fundscomma the Rural Development Fund or the Instrument forPre-Accession Assistance (IPA). The EC and the WB agree that more direct interaction would bebeneficial to both institutions and through them to the countries. Thisapplies particularly to the provision of analyticalcomma advisory andknowledge servicescomma capacity and institution buildingcomma and technicalassistancecomma but also to projects executed by respective governments.The EC has demonstrated its interest in specific analytical projects tobe carried out by the WB which provides guidance for investments in thelong-term prosperity and stability of the EU's Neighbourhood and support thereform process in those countries preparing for EU membership. Areas of common interest are regularly discussed and refined on theoccasion of sub-regional country day meetings between the services ofthe EC and WB that are held on an annual basis and reviewed by means ofan annual High-Level Dialogue with DG NEAR. These meetings have focusedon the Eastern Neighbourhoodcomma Central Asia and Pre-Accession countriescommaand on the developmental challenges faced in the Region and whichrequire a shared visioncomma coordinated efforts and complementarity ofactions. For the current MFF 2014-2020 the instruments offered by theECcomma and that the WB can help implement are: Instrument forPre-Accession Assistance (IPA)comma the European Neighbourhood Instrument(ENI)comma the Development Cooperation Instrument (DCI)comma the PartnershipInstrument (PI)comma and Macro-Financial Assistance (MFA). For the next MFF2021-2027comma the relevant instruments will be the NeighbourhoodcommaDevelopment and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI - 22billion for ECA Countries) and the Instrument for Pre-AccessionAssistance (IPA III - 14.5 billion)."
